scale.label: 30 mm heroic (about 32.5 mm to the crown)
scale.note: 30 mm from the soles to the visor line (eye convention, ratio from miniature_scale_convert); heroic power-armour proportions: broad 11 mm shoulders, armoured thighs and greaves, oversized gauntlets, helm and weapon.

catalog.revision_note: resin figure wearing the VH2-01 Lineguard helm, backpack and 25 mm base
catalog.base: 25 mm round deck-plate base, 3.8 mm, 5 × 2 mm magnet pocket
catalog.description: Revision 0.3 of the Vigilant rifleman: the Mk II advancing pose and reworked Lance bullpup, now wearing the second-generation VH2-01 Lineguard helm (gull-wing wrap visor split by the keel bar, layered crown and temple plates, V-prow respirator, cheek vents, aural hoses). The 0.1 and 0.2 riflemen are unchanged; any VH or VH2 helm swaps onto this body on the 1.6 mm D-flat peg.

images.label: Head close-up: VH2-01 on the figure

buildNotes: Sculpted as signed-distance fields (tools/sdfkit.py): smooth-blended anatomy, armour plates grown off the body and cut to oval outlines, panel lines engraved 0.25-0.4 mm deep.

Heroic scale: 30 mm to the visor line; the Lance rifle is 14 mm long with a 1.3 mm barrel, a 2.3 mm deep receiver and a box magazine behind the grip, thickened well past true scale so it prints and survives handling.
The figure stands on an integral 1.1 mm footplate that drops into a keyed recess in the base (0.1 mm glue clearance per side); no thin pins through the feet.

VH2-01 helm (tools/vh2.py) on a 1.6 mm D-flat peg (keyed to face along the rifle), backpack on a 2.0 mm D-flat peg: sizes from miniature_base_and_peg; every helm and pack in the line fits every figure.
Prints: figure tilted on supports at the angle miniature_support_plan picked, helm and backpack on supports, base flat on the plate (magnet pocket vented to the rim).
The Lance rifle (VW-01) is part of the figure; the same rifle ships as a loose bit in vigil-armory/print/stl (vw-01-lance-rifle.stl), sized to the line's gauntlet fists.
catalog.limitations: Procedural sculpt, not a hand sculpt: faces of the armour are smooth (no battle damage or texture), hands are gauntlet fists. Printability is a heuristic screen through unified-CAD-MCP, not a test print; the STEP is a faceted reference, not a parametric model.
